text:
Alex: Heads-up — who’s owning the launch window tomorrow at 17:00 PT? Need quick rollback readiness check.
Maria: I can take lead. timeline looks like 17:00–17:30 for canary, then ramp to 3 instances.
Alex: Perfect. Smoke checklist ready?
Maria: Short list: 1) healthcheck p95 < 250ms, 2) errors < 0.5% for 15m, 3) end-to-end payment flow test :white_check_mark:
Jamal: I added a synthetic test in staging -> job runs at 16:30, passes once before cutover.
Sophie: Rollback criteria: sustained error rate > 1% or latency spike > 2x baseline for 10m. Also DB migration fail -> immediate rollback.
Alex: How do we trigger rollback? manual only? auto?
Maria: Manual first. If deploy-bot sees fatal alerts we have auto-fallback to previous image after 5m — that's enabled for this release.
deploy-bot: auto-fallback policy is ENABLED for release/launch-orbit v3. Rollback command: `kubectl -n svc rollout undo deploy/api --to-revision=42`.
Jamal: Note: need to disable feature-flag `orbit-experiment` after rollback to avoid partial traffic.
Sophie: Who is on deck to run the rollback? Jamal / Maria team?
Maria: I’ll be the executor. Jamal will monitor metrics and Sophie will coordinate comms. Alex will approve go/no-go.
Alex: Acks. Add runbook link and the quick CLI we need.
Maria: Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/launch-orbit-rollback. Quick steps in case:
```
# get previous revision
kubectl -n svc rollout history deploy/api
kubectl -n svc rollout undo deploy/api --to-revision=<prev>
# flip feature flag
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/toggle -d '{"flag":"orbit-experiment","state":"off"}'
```
Maria: I'll post postmortem template to thread if we hit rollback.
Alex: Sounds good. If everyone is comfortable, give :thumbsup: and I'll lock in the 17:00 slot.
Jamal: :thumbsup:
Sophie: :thumbsup:
Maria: :thumbsup:
